latin: Ideo haec est falsa: Essentia generat, quia essentia est ultimate abstracta, et generat formaliter praedicatur. u
latin_note: The transcription at farmer1998:11974 appends an isolated letter 'u' after 'praedicatur.'; whether this belongs to the copy-text is not established by the sources consulted.
translation: Therefore this is false: 'The essence generates'; because the essence is utterly abstract, and 'generates' is predicated of it [only] formally.
translation_note: Edelheit's paraphrase gives the same sense: the proposition is false 'since essence is completely abstract, but it is formally predicated as ‘generating’' (edelheit2022:13078).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch5, from Latin at farmer1998:11974
attribution: Reports Francis of Meyronnes; farmer1998:11969 opens the eight-thesis section drawn from his commentary, of which this is the first (farmer1998:11974).

sources.text: Francis of Meyronnes, commentary on the Sentences, Book 1, distinction 5, question 1, 'whether the divine essence generates' (Utrum essentia divina generet)
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit identifies this question in Francis's commentary as the discussion behind the thesis.

doctrine: The thesis declares false the claim 'the essence generates,' on the ground that the essence is 'ultimately abstract' while 'generates' is predicated of it only formally (farmer1998:11974). Edelheit locates the source discussion in Francis of Meyronnes's commentary on the Sentences, Book 1, distinction 5, question 1, titled 'whether the divine essence generates' (edelheit2022:13078). Farmer's note glosses 'the essence' in this and the following thesis as the abstract divine nature considered apart from the three Persons, and records that Pico meant to set this essence alongside the Kabbalistic Ein-Sof and comparable concepts in other traditions (farmer1998:12005).
context: Farmer's note ties 3.1-3.2 to his comments on 2.1 (Trinitarian procession, from Thomas) and 11>4 (the Kabbalistic Ein-Sof), which suggests Pico read Francis's logic of the divine essence alongside both the Thomist and Kabbalistic material (farmer1998:12005).
historiography: Edelheit treats the thesis as the first of a run he attributes to Francis of Meyronnes's commentary on Sentences Book 1, and observes that Pico's opening word 'ideo' ('therefore') implies a continuation from a preceding discussion, 'possibly the previous set of theses, those dedicated to Thomas, and probably the last one, thesis 45' (edelheit2022:13099).

quotations.text: In thesis 1 we find that the proposition ‘essence generates’ is false since essence is completely abstract, but it is formally predicated as ‘generating’.

But why this thesis opens with the adverb ideo (therefore), suggesting a continuation from a previous discussion, possibly the previous set of theses, those dedicated to Thomas, and probably the last one, thesis 45?

not_established: Whether the isolated 'u' after 'praedicatur' in the inventory's transcription belongs to Farmer's text is not established by the sources consulted.
